rows.author: D032
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO INCLUDE THE TEACHING OF THE CONSTITUTION AS PART OF THE SCHOOL CURRICULUM IN THE SECONDARY LEVEL
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to include the teaching of the Constitution as part of the school curriculum in the secondary level. It is the foremost intention of this measure to inculcate in the youth, the fair hope of the fatherland, patriotism and nationalismand to apprise them of their constitutionall y guaranteed rights and obligations to make them responsible and law-abiding citizens of the country.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-25

rows.author: D032
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZ ING FREE PUBLIC PREPARATORY EDUCATION, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Free Public Preparatory Educations means that the children from five (5) to six (6) years old enrolled in day care centers established, administered, maintained and funded by national and local government units, and those public preparatory schoolswhich may be established by law, shall be free from payment of tuition and other school fees. These qualified children shall finish one (1) year of schooling before they are admitted to Grade I.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PRE-NEED PLAN CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: It is the policy of the State to regulate the establishment of pre-need companies and to place their operation on a sound, efficient and stable basis to derive the optimum advantages from them in the mobilization of savings and to preventand mitigate, as far as practicable, practices prejudicial to public interest and the protection of planholders.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05535

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROTECTION AND CONSERVATION OF ALL OBJECTS OF UNDERWATER CULTURAL HERITAGE IN PHILIPPINE WATER
rows.abstract: This bill aims to protect and preserve our underwater cultural heritage by providing for general requirements for underwater archaeology, exploration, and excavation, the description of the items to be protected, prohibition of certain activities inthe vicinity of a protected item and site, the establishment of a reward system for verified reports, and the imposition of sanction/penalt ies for violations.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-25

rows.author: B001
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING TO THE PUBLIC A PEOPLE'S FRANKING PRIVILEGE ON COMMUNICATIONS MAILED OR SENT BY CABLE/TELEGRAM TO THE PRESIDENT, VICE PRESIDENT, SENATORS, MEMBERS OF THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES AND TO CABINET SECRETARIES
rows.abstract: All communications, whether by mail or cable/telegram from the public addressed to the President, Vice-President, Senators, Members of the House of Representatives and Cabinet Secretaries for delivery within the country shall be received, transmitted and delivered free of charge; Provided, that the mail shall be sent by ordinary mail only; Provided further, that the said mail shall not exceed one hundred twenty grams in weight; and Provided finally, that cables and telegrams shall be sent through government telegraph offices.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2001-07-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE PHILIPPINE RUBBER DEVELOPMENT BOARD, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill would finally ensure growth and expansion of the rubber industry as there will now be a government body, through the Philippine Rubber Development Board, that would carry our pertinent policies and programs towards the end of fully developing the rubber industry, following the success stories of Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.

rows.abstract: Rationale: The State shall ensure that all sectors of society benefit from its development programs as well as guarantee and protect the interests of those who belong to minority groups, especially the Filipino Muslims and shall extend to them the highest level of development efforts as well as secure the preservation of the rich cultural heritage of these people.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06291

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT RECOGNIZING THE POTENTIALS OF THE FILIPINO YOUTH TOWARD NATION BUILDING, PRESCRIBING THE FREE EXERCISE OF CERTAIN RIGHTS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Magna Carta for Youth". Rationale: All efforts shall be exerted by the State to remove any form of prejudices against the youth. The State shall continue to extend full support for the youth's total well-being and for their consequent recognition as "the nation's only hope for the future". Government in all levels shall adopt policies ensuring their empowerment, emancipation, self-reliance and development through the enhancement of their skills and potentials that will enable them to compete favorably for available opportunities, become significant contributors to national progress and foster more meaningful, productive and satisfying life.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on YOUTH AND SPORTS DEVELOPMENT since 2001-07-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ESTABLISH CERTAIN LIMITATIONS ON ADVERTISING RELATING TO CIGARETTES AND TOBACCO PRODUCTS
rows.abstract: "Tobacco Products Control Act". Rationale: Thousands of Filipinos have already died and are continuously suffering from smoking-related diseases. Unless concrete measures are taken, such malady is expected to further worsen. Hence this bill.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05950

first_reading.comm_act: chnge of cttee. ref'l from Public Info as per J. 67; p.30

rows.author: C020
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09211) enacted on 2003-06-23
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO RESTRICT THE ACCESS OF YOUTH TO CIGARETTES AND OTHER TOBACCO PRODUCTS
rows.abstract: "Control Youth Access to Tobacco Act". Some restrictions provided in this bill are: (1) MINIMUM AGE - No manufacturer, distributor, or retailer or tobacco products may offer or distribute tobacco products may sell a tobacco product to an individualwho is less than 18 years old; (2) PACKAGES OF CIGARETTES - Only cigarettes in a package of 20 cigarettes may be sold or distributed by a manufacturer, distributor, or retailer or tobacco products; and (3) SAMPLING - No manufacturer, distributor, orretailer or tobacco products may offer or distribute tobacco products for sampling except in an area or establishment from which minors are denied access.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05950

rows.abstract: Rationale: Monetary benefits received by employees in the course of their separation from work for causes such as termination are treated as income of these employees. As such, they are assessed the corresponding tax rate.

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 285 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, PROVIDING FOR THE REDUCTION OF THE INTERNAL REVENUE ALLOCATION (IRAs) OF HIGH-INCOME LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS (LGUs) BY EIGHT PERCENTAGE (8%) FOR THE BENEFIT OF LOW INCOME LGUs
rows.abstract: To make the present system of IRA allocation more responsive to the needs of low-income LGUs, this bill proposes to reduce the IRAs of high-income LGUs for the benefit of low-income LGUs. The reduced IRA will be allocated in proportion to populationdensity, poverty incidence, and income class of LGUs, in lieu of land area and equal sharing.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 284 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS "THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991", AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "SEC. 284. Allotment of Internal Revenue Taxes - Local government units shall have a share in the national revenue taxes based on the collection of the third fiscal year preceding the current fiscal year as follows: (a) On the first year of the effectivity of this Code, thirty percent (30%); (b) On the second year, thirty-five percent (35%); and (c) On the third year and thereafter, fifty percent (50%).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT ABOLISHING THE DEATH PENALTY AND IMPOSING THE PENALTY OF QUALIFIED RECLUSION PERPETUA IN LIEU THEREOF, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7659 OR THE DEATH PENALTLAW, ACT 3815, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE, AS AMENDED, ANDOTHER SPECIAL LAWS

rows.abstract: Any person sentenced to Qualified Reclusion Perpetua shall serve his sentence until his natural death without benefit of loyalty and good conduct allowance, commutation, parole or pardon.  All persons who have been meted out the death penalty by final judgement shall have their sentences commuted to Qualified Reclusion Perpetua.

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE NATIONAL AGRARIAN REFORM ADJUDICATION COMMISSION, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: Despite the good intentions behind its creation, the DARAB is beset with serious structural flaws, specifially, with respect to its composition and its capacity to effectively discharge its mandated tasks. To remedy this situation, this bill proposes to create the NARAC which shall have jurisdiction over all agrarian disputes. Its adjudicatory functions shall be exercised through five (5) divisions, acting independently of each other.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRARIAN REFORM since 2001-07-25

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO REWARD INFORMANTS WHO HELP IDENTIFY, LOCATE AND RECOVER ANY ILL-GOTTEN WEALTH OF THE LATE PRESIDENT FERDINAND E. MARCOS, AND HIS WIDOW, IMELDA R. MARCOS AND OTHER DEFENDANTS/RESP ONDENTS IN ILL-GOTTEN WEALTH CASES WHEREVER LOCATED AND BY WHOMSOEVER HELD AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: One of the reasons for the dismal record of recovery of the PCGG is that it never seemed to have gotten the support of the people. From the looks of it, if PCGG was left to its own devices, it would probably find the recovery process getting rougher as years pass by with very little tangible results to prod it to go on or even justify its continued existence. Perhaps, by adopting a system of reward for those who provide the government with credible and relevant information on the whereabouts of the Marcos hidden or ill-gotten wealth, the people might just get their hands on it sooner than later.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-07-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT TOTALLY BANNING LOGGING OPERATIONS FOR THE NEXT TWENTY-FIVE (25) YEARS
rows.abstract: It shall be unlawful for any person to cut, fell or destroy any tree standing on any forest, timber land, forest reserve or watershed within the next twenty-five (25) years from the approval of this Act. This prohibition shall not apply to trees grown in legitimate commercial tree farms.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05162

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE TEACHING OF HUMAN RIGHTS AS MANDATORY IN ALL PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SCHOOLS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: All public and private shools shall include human rights courses in their curricula. No school shall be established or allowed to operate unless this requirement is complied with. The Department of Education, Culture and Sports, in consultation withthe Commission on Human rights, shall formulate courses on human rights to be taught as separate courses or incorporated in existing subjects now being taught in all levels of education throughout the country.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-25

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE PROPER USE OF HANDHELD RADIOS AND MOBILE TELEPHONES WHILE DRIVING ANY KIND OF VEHICLES, PRESCRIBING PENALTY THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: An act shall constitute a violation to the provision of this Act when the driver uses and/or operates his/her handheld band radio and/or mobile telephone in the course of driving in any private or public street, road or highway; Provided, That the act of using or operating the handheld band radio and/or mobile telephone is simultaneously done while the driven vehicle is in motion. This, however, is subject to certain requirements.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2001-07-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT BANNING THE ISSUANCE AND USE OF LOW-NUMBERED PROTOCOL CARPLATES ON VEHICLES OF RANKING GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS
rows.abstract: The issuance and use of low-numbered car plates for vehicles of ranking government officials are hereby banned. All low-numbered car plates starting from No. 2, all the way down to the numbers now being assigned to Cabinet members and bureau directors issued in the past are hereby cancelled and deemed withdrawn

rows.abstract: This bill seeks to give recognition to Filipino athletes who have brought honor and prestige to the country by winning gold, silver and bronze medals in the Olympic Games, Asian Games, SEA Games and other international championships by giving them cash awards.

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING COUNTRYSIDE CREDIT THROUGH COOPERATIVE BANKS AND ENCOURAGING THE GROWTH AND DEVELOPMENT OF COOPERATIVE BANKS BY AMENDING CHAPTER XIII OF THE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6938, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE COOPERATIVE CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AND FOROTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill provides for the strengthening of the cooperative banking system in the country, particularly in rural and remote areas where credit and financial services are solely needed. Toward this end, the bill extends a package  of incentives, whichare at present enjoyed by thrift banks under Republic Act No. 7906 and rural banks under Republic Act No. 7353.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05206

rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE TRANSFER OF OFFENDERS TO OR FROM FOREIGN COUNTRIES
rows.abstract: This bill shall only applicable to the transfer of an offender to and from a foreign country pursuant to a treaty that is in force: Provided, That a sentence imposed by a foreign court upon an offender who is subsequently transferred to the Philippines pursuant to a treaty shall be fully executed in the Philippines even though the treaty under which the offender was transferred is no longer in force.

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE FIELD OF LAND TITLE INSURANCE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 612, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE INSURANCE CODE OF 1978 AS AMENDED BY PRESIDENTIAL DECREES NOS. 1455 AND 1460 AND BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 874
rows.abstract: This type of insurance guarantees a potential buyer of real estate or one loaning money on mortgage that the property in question is free from any title defect. This will serve to increase the confidence of real estate buyers or mortgages over the Torrens Title since they are assured that title insurance would guarantee them some form of compensation should a defect in the land title later be discovered.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2001-07-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING ASSISTANCE TO PRIVATE HOSPITALS BY GRANTING INCENTIVES AND ESTABLISHING A PRIVATE-HOSPITA L DEVELOPMENT PLAN
rows.abstract: This bill proposes a Private Hospital Development Plan which will be drawn in coordination with the Secretary of Health, appropriate government agencies and non-governmenta l organizations. This plan shall monitor the needs of private hospitals in terms of its facilities, equipment and human resources. It shall also grant tax incentives to accredited private hospitals.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A COST SHARING SCHEME TO PROVIDE FOR A HOSPITAL CARE PROGRAM IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to institutionaliz e a local health delivery system among local governments to solve the problem of access to medical care. The will require local government units to establish a cost sharing scheme that will provide hospitalizationservices to their constituents. The system will not only provide hospitalization but also include blood typing of all residents for easy access to blood donors and establish a perfect system of identity of all citizens of the country.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 26, CHAPTER 4, BOOK VI OF THE ADMINISTRATIVE CODE OF 1987
rows.abstract: "SEC. 26. Automatic Appropriations. - All expenditures for Personnel Retirement Premiums, Government Service, Insurance, and other similar Fixed Expenditures are automatically appropriated: Provided, That no obligations shall be incurred or interests made from funds thus automatically appropriated except as issued in form of Regular Budgetary Allotments."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-25

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING BUSINESS ONE-STOP SHOP (BOSS) CENTERS FOR SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES IN ALL REGIONAL AND PROVINCIAL CENTERS IN THE COUNTRY
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to remedy one problem in business start-ups, by making it easier for entrepreneurs and propsective entrepreneurs to fulfill the documentary requirements of starting a business enterprise. This it does by mandating all government agencies taking a hand in business start-ups to situate themselves through a branch or satellite office in the so-called Business One-Stop-Shop or BOSS Center.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECONOMIC AFFAIRS since 2001-07-25

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-05-23, transmitted to on 2002-05-28 and received by the Senate on 2002-05-28
rows.title_full: AN ACT RENAMING THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AS THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FISHERIES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Sometimes, name change can make a difference in underscoring official policy. One such renaming is that of the Department of Agriculture to include the Fisheries sector, since the latter constitutes a very significant component of our country's economy. By so doing, the government serves notice that the sector is also a very important one in the allocation of scarce government resources.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04467

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: Business for the day on 2004-01-27
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A COLLEGE EDUCATION TRUST FUND FOR CHILDREN OF GSIS AND SSS MEMBERS
rows.abstract: This bill proposes to further broaden opportunities for higher education by enabling qualified SSS and GSIS members to insure the college education of their children through the College Education Trust Fund created under this Act. This fund consistsof the premiums paid by the Member. This bill seeks to guarantee the completion of a basic four-year or five-year college course.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06641

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE USE OF RECYCLABLE OR BIODEGRADABLE MATERIALS FOR THE PACKAGING OF CONSUMER PRODUCTS
rows.abstract: The State declares as policy the conservation and preservation of nature. In this respect, the use of recyclable and biodegradable materials is mandated in the manufacturing process of consumer goods. Any business or non-business entity which shallundertake the effort of using recyclable and biodegradable materials for the packaging of consumer goods shall enjoy a tax deductibility privilege on its income tax to the extent of the proven cost of the recyclable or biodegradable materials for thepackaging of consumer goods shall enjoy a tax deductibility privilege on its income tax to the extent of the proven cost of the recyclable or biodegradable material on its production process.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-07-25

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09211) enacted on 2003-06-23
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING ALL CIGARETTE AND CIGAR MANUFACTURERS AND DISTRIBUTORS TO SCIENTIFICALLY DETERMINE AND TRUTHFULLY PRINT, ON EACH BOX OR PACK OF CIGARS OR CIGARETTES THAT THEY MANUFACTURE, DISTRIBUTE OR SELL WITHIN THE COUNTRY, THE LEVELS OF NICOTINE, TAR AND CARBON MONOXIDE THAT COULD BE INHALED IN SMOKING A STICK OF CIGAR OR CIGARETTE, AND PROVIDE PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF
rows.abstract: Rationale: The purpose is to enable smokers or potential smokers to at least know precisely how much nicotine, tar and deadly carbon monoxide could be imbibed in smoking cigars or cigarettes. Such information may provide fair warning on the health risks of smoking as well as provide data on the amount of toxins spread by smokers on so-called secondary smoke.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05950

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING MEASURES TO ENSURE PEDESTRIAN SAFETY AND CONVENIENCE
rows.abstract: "Pedestrian Safety Law". This bill aims to address four different but related areas of public concern: (1) the worsening traffice conditions in our cities; (2) the corresponding congestion along our sidewalks; (3) the guarantee of safe and convenient public access for all pedestrian, especially the disabled; and (4) the absence if adequate relief for pedestrians who suffer damage as a result of hazards to passage along our roads and sidewalks.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 2001-07-25

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MODERNIZATION OF THE NATIONAL MAPPING AND RESOURCE INFORMATION AUTHORITY (NAMRIA); AMENDING CERTAIN PORTIONS OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 192, SECTION 22(a) AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill is premised on the State policy to promote and pursue the modernization of the National Mapping and Resource Information Authority (NAMRIA) to a level where it can effectively and fully perform its mandate to act as the official surveyingand mapping agency of the Republic of the Philippines, and provide the government and the private sector with reliable geographic information.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY since 2001-07-25

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE CONSERVATION AND PROTECTION OF WILDLIFE RESOURCES AND THEIR HABITATS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This proposed measure aims to: (1) to conserve and protect wildlife species and their habitats to promote ecological balance and enhance biological diversity; (2) to regulate the collection and trade of wildlife; (3) to pursue, with due regard to the national interest, the Philippine commitment to international conventions, protection of wildlife and their habitats; and (4) to initiate or support scientific studies on the conservation of biological diversity.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2001-07-25

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09257) enacted on 2004-03-03
rows.title_full: THE MAGNA CARTA FOR OLDER PERSONS
rows.abstract: This bill is premised on a number of principles, principally one of which is older persons are part of Philippine society, thus the State shall give full support to the improvement of the total well-being of the elderly and their full participationin society. Toward this end, the State shall adopt policies ensuring the health, rahabilitation and self-reliance of older persons.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05987

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A FIVE(5)-YEAR PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS INFRASTRUCTURE PROGRAM
rows.abstract: This bill proposes a 5-year master plan of infrastructure building in the country. The bill aims for continuity and establishing of our public works spending by laying out the specific investment areas and targets.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 2001-07-25

rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-11-29, transmitted to on 2002-12-02 and received by the Senate on 2002-12-04
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT OF FOREST RESOURCES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill proposes a framework for the SUSTAINABLE management of our forests by promoting the participation of all sectors of society. It seeks to establishment people-oriented forest service that shall benefit the people and the country to the fullest.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05162

rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE REORGANIZATION OF THE EXECUTIVE BRANCH AND OTHER RELATED PURPOSE
rows.abstract: Rationale: There is a need to review government's role vis-a-vis the people's aspirations for freedom from want, from hunger, from ignorance, from fear and from disease. There is a need to review how government can make rights and freedom in a democracy become secure foundations upon which the people can participate fully and actively in the building of a democratic society. There is a need to give flesh to the ideal that government be a visible, competent, efficient and accessible partner of the people both in their daily quests for survival towards a better life and in bringing to fruition their hopes for a more confident future.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2001-07-25

first_reading.comm_act: jt. ref'l as per J.37; p.19

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING ONE STEP SALARY GRADE INCREASE TO GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES ONE(1)-YEAR BEFORE COMPULSORY RETIREMENT AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: A one step salary grade increase in the basic salaries of government employees in the year before their retirement will ensure an increase in lump sum retirement benefits and monthly pensions that they can use to engage in useful enterprise that will benefit them and their community during the remaining years of their lives.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-07-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE COMPUTATION OF RETIREMENT BENEFITS OF GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES AND OFFICIALS WHO COMPULSORILY RETIRE FROM THE SERVICE ON THE BASIS OF THE SALARY GRADE NEXT HIGHER TO THE SALARY GRADE CORRESPONDING TO THEIR POSITION AT THE TIME OF THEIR RETIREMENT AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The retirement benefits inclusive of pensions, gratuities and similar benefits granted to government employees and officials who compulsorily retire from government service shall be computed on the basis of the next higher salary grade to the salarygrade corresponding to the position they are holding at the time of their retirement.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-07-25

rows.author: B012
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE SALE THROUGH PUBLIC AUCTION OF ALL KINDS OF CONFISCATED SMUGGLED GOODS AND PRODUCTS AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: Smuggled goods and products, after liability to seizure or forfeiture shall have been established by proper administrative or judicial proceeding in conformity with the provisions of the Tariff and Customs Code, shall be burned or destroyed in suchmanner as to render them absolutely useless or worthless.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-07-25

rows.author: B012
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE MONTHLY RETIREMENT PENSION OF ALL SOCIAL SECURITY SYSTEM (SSS) RETIREES TO A MINIMUM LEVEL OF SIX THOUSAND (P6,000.00) PESOS UNDER AN ECONOMIC ADJUSTMENT PENSION PROGRAM
rows.abstract: This bill shall provide for the adjustment of Social Security System monthly pension to Three Thousand Pesos (P3,000), provided that in the succeeding years upon approval of this Act, said amount will be increased annualy by not less than One Thousand Five-Hundred Pesos (P1,500) until the total monthly pension shall be at least Six Thousand Pesos (P6,000) per month.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2001-07-25

rows.author: B012
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING DISCRIMINATION IN THE RECRUITMENT, EMPLOYMENT, PROMOTION AND DISMISSAL OF ANY MEMBER OF THE THIRD SEX BOTH IN PUBLIC AND PRIVATE EMPLOYMENT AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Any provision of existing laws to the contrary notwithstanding , it shall be unlawful for an employer to discriminate against any member of the third sex with regards to their recruitment, employment, promotion and dismissal both in public and private employment.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-07-25

rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-25

rows.status: Substituted by HB05346

rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING FOOD AND DRINK THAT DEVELOP OBESITY AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: All food and drink with great amount of calories as determined by the Department of Health are hereby regulated in its manufacture, distribution, sale or consumption.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-07-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND SECTION 61 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBERED ONE THOUSAND FOUR HUNDRED AND FORTY-FIVE, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE `GOVERNMENT AUDITING CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES' AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to exempt certain government expense accounts from the standard auditing procedures and techniques to be followed and the extent of examination of vouchers and other documents by government auditors.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING FREE SPECIAL EDUCATION CLASSES FOR THE PHYSICALLY DISABLED PERSONS WHO WILL ENROLL IN ALL PUBLIC ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY SCHOOLS OF THE COUNTRY, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: Physically disabled persons have a right to the quality of education that will suit their needs and develop their potentials to the maximum. For the disabled, sophisticated and modern teaching-learnn g materials are virtually unheard of.And on occations where there may be special classes conducted by the nongovernmental organizations and private sector, the teacher may either lack the necessary proper training for such a specialized purpose or the use of teaching methods designed for disabled persons.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING LEGAL ASSISTANCE TO MEMBERS OF THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES AND THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE CHARGED FOR SERVICE-CONNECT ED OFFENSES AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The Secretary of National Defense and the Secretary of the Interior and Local Government may authorize lawyers of their respective departments to provide legal assistance and representation to any member of the Armed Forces of the Philippines and the Philippine National Police who is facing charges before fiscals and courts for any offense arising from or connected with the performance of his official duties. Should government lawyers be not readily available, lawyers from the private sectors may be hired to provide such legal assistance.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE since 2001-07-25

rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-05-23, transmitted to on 2002-05-28 and received by the Senate on 2002-05-28
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE LEGITIMATION OF CHILDREN BORN TO PARENTS BELOW MARRYING AGE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Only children conceived and born outside of wedlock of parents who, at the time of the conception of the former, were not disqualified by any impediment to marry each other EXCEPT BY REASON OF AGE, may be legitimated.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04538

rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING APRIL 22 OF EVERY YEAR AS `EARTH DAY' AND PROVIDING GUIDELINES FOR ITS OBSERVANCE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: For the observance of this occasion, each year, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources, in coordination with the Philippine Information Agency, shall conduct an information campaign on the serious global threats posed by environmental pollution and over-exploitati on of natural resources. The Department of Education, Culture and Sports shall require school, colleges and universities to conduct lectures/semina rs, for contests and other means to foster awareness among their studentson the above-mentioned subject matter.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-25

rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2003-02-10, transmitted to on 2003-02-11 and received by the Senate on 2003-02-13
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING FIELD OFFICES OF THE BUREAU OF FOOD AND DRUGS IN PROVINCES AND CITIES AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: Food, drugs and cosmetics can contribute to the well-being or to the deterioration of a person's health. To ensure safety and purity of food, drugs and cosmetics, there should be established an office which implements the State policy onsafeguarding the health of the populace.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05497

rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09211) enacted on 2003-06-23
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING SMOKING IN PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION AND BUILDINGS, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Smoking is strictly prohibited in public transportation and buildings. For purposes of this bill, smoking shall include cigars and cigarette smoking and pipe smoking or any device creating cigarette or tobacco fumes. Any person who violates this bill shall be punished by imprisonment of not less than five or more than ten (10) days or a fine of not less than Five Hundred Pesos (P500.00) nore more than One Thousand Pesos (P1,000.00) or both such imprisonment and fine at the discreation of the court.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05950

first_reading.comm_act: chnge of cttee. ref'l from Health as per J. 67; p.30

rows.mother_status: Consigned to the Archives on 2003-12-09
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING THAT A SUBJECT IN PARAPSYCHOLOGY BE INCORPORATED IN THE SCHOOL CURRICULA OF ALL PRIVATE AND PUBLIC HIGH SCHOOLS AND COLLEGES IN THE COUNTRY
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to include parapsychology in the curriculum to enable the youth to widen their educational horizon and perspectives. It will help them understand occurrences or phenomena outside the natural order of things. Likewise, parapsychologyas a subject in the curriculum will enable individuals with this natural ability to develop their psychic and extraordinary powers for their over-all advancement.
rows.status: Substituted by HR01097

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROVIDE A SPEEDY PROCEDURE IN THE DISBURSEMENT OF FUNDS DURING PERIODS OF CALAMITY BY AMENDING SECTION 287, TITLE THREE, CHAPTER 1, OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Each local government unit shall appropriate in an annual budget no less than twenty percent (20%) of its annual revenue allotment for development projects. Copies of the development plans of local government units shall be furnished the Departmentof Interior and Local Government; PROVIDED, THAT IN THE EVENT OF A CALAMITY, THE AMOUNT APPROPRIATED FOR DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS SHALL BE USED TO COVER THE RELIEF AND REHABILITATION EXPENSES OF THE PROVINCE, CITY OR MUNICIPALITY, SUBJECT TO REIMBURSEMENT BY THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT ADOPTING COMMUNITY SERVICE AS AN ALTERNATIVE PENALTY FOR CERTAIN OFFENSES IN LIEU OF DEPRIVATION OF LIBERTY OR PAYMENT OF FINE
rows.abstract: "Community Service Law of 2001." "Community Service" a type of penalty in lieu of imprisonment or fine by which the offender at any time before conviction and sentence is released subject to conditions imposed by the court and to the supervision ofthe community service officer. For purpose of this bill, community service shall, include but shall not be limited to tree planting, street sweeping, participation in livelihood and environmental rehabilitation projects and other government assistedprojects for the welfare of the community.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-25
